summary: Giuliana Martini works in Buddhist studies. In 2010, she held posts at both the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University.

Giuseppe Bardelli (1815–1865) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He served as a lecturer in Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa from circa 1845 to 1849.

Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti (1774–1849) was a linguist who studied at the University of Bologna. He served at the University of Bologna as a professor across 1797–1831 and became Custodian-in-Chief at the Vatican Library in 1833.

Giuseppe Tucci (1894–1984) was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Sapienza University of Rome, Visva-Bharati, Dhaka, and BHU. He taught at Rome and served as president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

Giuseppe Vignato specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He completed doctoral studies at Peking University under Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Bai Su, and Shichang Ma, and was attested as holding a post at Peking University in 2017.

Giyu Nishi (1897–1993) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He held a post at the University of Tokyo in 1926 and became a professor at Toyo University in 1927.

Glenn H. Mullin (born 1949) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama, and founded the Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.
Glenn Wallis is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Godabarish Mishra (1886–1956) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta. He taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya, was headmaster at Chakradharpur High School, and served as Director at the University of Madras.

Gombojab Tsybikov (1873–1930) was a scholar of Tibetology and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University, and served as a Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University from circa 1902 to 1917.
Gopal Lal Meena is an Indologist. Attested in 2026, he held posts as Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Professor emeritus at the University of Delhi.

Gopinath Kaviraj (1887–1976) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. Educated at Maharaja's College and the University of Allahabad under Arthur Venis, he held multiple posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, including librarian, Principal, and Head of Yoga-Tantra.

Gordon D. Kaufman (1925–2011) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher who studied at Bethel College, Northwestern University, and Yale University. He held posts at Pomona College, Vanderbilt University, and as Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity at Harvard Divinity School.

Gordon Hannington Luce (1889–1979) was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist. He studied at Emmanuel College, Cambridge, and served as a professor at the University of Rangoon from circa 1920 to 1964.

Gordon Johnson (born 1943) is a historian and Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as fellow at Trinity and Selwyn Colleges, President of Wolfson College, Cambridge, and Deputy Vice-Chancellor of the University of Cambridge.

Gore Ouseley (1770–1844) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He served in the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (circa 1810–1815) and as Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (circa 1823–1844).

Gottfried August Bürger (1747–1794) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1768 to 1772 and later held a post there from circa 1784 to 1794.

Gottfried Bernhardy (1800–1875) was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1817 to 1820, he held a post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1829 to 1875.

Gottfried Ernst Groddeck (1762–1824) was a linguist and historian who studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen. He served as a professor at Vilnius University from circa 1804 until 1824.

Gottfried Hermann (1772–1848) was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig and the University of Jena. He served at the University of Leipzig as an extraordinary professor of philosophy in 1798 and as director of the philological seminar from 1803 to 1848.
